fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Wisdom teeth are the last teeth to develop, usually emerging in the late teens or early twenties. For some people, they come through without issue. For others, there is not enough room, and wisdom teeth can become stuck, erupt at an angle or cause pain, infection and damage to nearby teeth.

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: At Precision Dental, we assess your wisdom teeth carefully and give you honest advice about whether they should be monitored or removed.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Are Wisdom Teeth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Wisdom teeth are the third molars, located at the very back of the mouth. Most people have four, although some have fewer or none at all.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: When a wisdom tooth does not have enough space to erupt fully, it is described as impacted. Impacted wisdom teeth may be partially visible through the gum or remain entirely hidden within the jawbone. They can grow at various angles, sometimes pressing against the tooth in front.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Is Wisdom Teeth Removal Right for You?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Not every wisdom tooth needs to be removed. Removal may be recommended if you experience:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Pain or swelling at the back of the mouth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Repeated gum infections around a partially erupted tooth, known as pericoronitis

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Decay in the wisdom tooth or the neighbouring molar

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Damage to the tooth in front

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Difficulty cleaning around the wisdom tooth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Cysts or other changes seen on X-rays

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: If your wisdom teeth are healthy, fully erupted and easy to clean, we may simply monitor them at your regular check-ups. Teenagers and young adults may benefit from an assessment as part of preventive care for young adults.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Assessment and Imaging

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We examine the area and take a digital OPG, a panoramic X-ray that shows all of your teeth, the position and angle of your wisdom teeth, and their relationship to nearby nerves and sinuses. Additional 3D imaging may be recommended in some cases.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Discussing Your Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We explain what we see, the benefits and risks of removal or monitoring, and the costs involved. Depending on the complexity of your case, removal may be performed at our practice, or we may refer you to an oral and maxillofacial surgeon, particularly where treatment under general anaesthetic is more appropriate.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Removal at Our Practice

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: For suitable cases, wisdom teeth are removed under local anaesthetic, with happy gas available to help you relax. Some teeth can be removed in one piece, while others need to be sectioned. Stitches may be placed, and you will receive written aftercare instructions.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Swelling and discomfort are common for several days and usually peak around the second or third day. Use cold compresses, take pain relief as advised, and eat soft, cool foods. Avoid smoking, straws, alcohol and vigorous rinsing for the first 24 hours. From the following day, rinse gently with warm salt water. Contact us if you have increasing pain after a few days, persistent bleeding, fever, or numbness that does not resolve.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for Wisdom Teeth

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for Wisdom Teeth

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We use digital OPG imaging to assess your wisdom teeth accurately, and we always give honest advice about whether removal is necessary. When a referral is more appropriate, we tell you why. For those who feel nervous, happy gas can make treatment more comfortable.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Interest-free payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Do all wisdom teeth need to be removed?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. Healthy wisdom teeth that are well positioned and easy to clean may simply be monitored.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: At what age should wisdom teeth be assessed?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: An assessment in the mid to late teens is often helpful, as it allows us to monitor development before problems arise.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How long is recovery after wisdom teeth removal?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Most people feel better within about a week, although it varies. Surgical removal of impacted teeth may take longer to recover from.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will I be asleep during the procedure?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: At our practice, removal is performed under local anaesthetic, with happy gas available. If general anaesthetic is more suitable, we can refer you to an oral surgeon.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: What are the risks of wisdom teeth removal?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Risks include pain, swelling, infection, dry socket and, particularly with lower wisdom teeth, a small risk of temporary or permanent numbness. We discuss these with you before treatment.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can I use my super for wisdom teeth removal?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: In some circumstances, early release of superannuation may be available for eligible patients. Services such as SuperCare can help you explore eligibility.
